transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... I guess I'm here because I've been having a little bit of trouble just, you know, staying in one place? 

I've been trying really hard to just tough it out—for months now, really—but whenever I'm supposed to sit still in the radiology suite at work, or during my classes, I just... I get this feeling like I'm crawling out of my skin. I don't mean to be disruptive or anything, I swear, but I always end up shifting around in my seat, or pacing, or just finding some excuse to get up and move. I'm really trying to do better with it, but it's been kind of overwhelming. Does that make sense to talk about here?
Are you currently taking any prescription medications?

Oh, um, no. No, I'm not taking any prescription medications right now. I usually try to just... you know, manage things on my own if I can? I hope that's okay. I mean, I'm generally pretty healthy otherwise, I promise. 

Is that alright? Or, um, did you need me to list out like, over-the-counter stuff or vitamins? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.
Is this uncomfortable sensation or urge to move mainly focused in your legs, or does it feel like your whole body?

Oh, um... I don't think it's just my legs? I hope I'm answering this right, but it feels more like... like my whole body, I guess? 

It's just this overall feeling of being kind of wired. It's not like my legs are hurting or tingling or anything bad like that, I promise. It's just this general urge where my whole self just wants to get up and do something. Does that make sense? I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it very well, I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you find that you spend a lot of time worrying about many different everyday things, and find it hard to control that worry?

Um, worrying? I mean, I guess I worry a normal amount, just like anyone else would? 

I don't think I spend a lot of time stressing over things, really. I try to stay pretty positive and just keep busy, you know? I definitely don't feel like I'm out of control with it or anything like that. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just don't want to make it sound like I'm anxious all the time when I'm really not. Is it okay if I don't really have that problem?
Did you have similar difficulties with restlessness or sitting still when you were a child, before the age of 12?

Oh, um... yeah, I guess I did? I hope it's okay to admit that. I really wasn't trying to be a bad kid or be disrespectful to my teachers, I promise! 

But, um... my parents actually still talk about these elementary school parent-teacher conferences we used to have. They said the teachers would always tell them I was constantly out of my seat, or calling out answers, or rushing ahead to do things before the directions were even finished. 

So, yeah, it was definitely happening way before middle school... it's not just something that started recently since I got into my radiology training. I just always had a lot of energy, I guess? I hope that's the right kind of information. Did that answer your question okay?
